saints.name: St. Teresa of Calcutta
saints.title: Religious and Foundress
saints.shortBlurb: The little Albanian sister who left the classroom for the slums of Calcutta and made the dying poor her whole life…
biography: Born Anjezë Gonxhe Bojaxhiu at Skopje in 1910, she joined the Sisters of Loreto and taught in Calcutta before receiving, in 1946, what she called a "call within a call" to serve the poorest of the poor. In 1950 she founded the Missionaries of Charity, gathering the abandoned, the sick, and the dying from the streets to die with dignity.

Her work spread across the world and won her the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979, though she remained a small figure in a white sari. She died in Calcutta in 1997; her private writings later revealed a long interior darkness borne in faith. She was canonized by Pope Francis in 2016.
saints.knownFor: Serving Christ in the poorest of the poor through the Missionaries of Charity.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Teresa of Calcutta (vatican.va)
